title: Equal product prominence
acceptance_criteria: both journeys are reachable within one deliberate action from the hero and mobile menu.

title: Discovery and accessibility
acceptance_criteria: keyboard, empty, loading, error and mobile states are covered for every primary route.

title: Public search
acceptance_criteria: unpublished content and customer drafts never appear; a curated 50-query relevance test meets its agreed pass threshold.

title: Discoverability and honesty
acceptance_criteria: no fictional testimonials, customers, ratings or regulator endorsements are displayed in production.

title: Real customer identity
acceptance_criteria: verification, expired-link, logout, recovery and suspended-account tests pass.

title: Secure sessions and privileged access
acceptance_criteria: revoked sessions cannot call private endpoints; staff role changes are audited.

title: Tenant boundaries
acceptance_criteria: changing a workspace, draft, order or file identifier cannot reveal another business’s data.

title: Business profile
acceptance_criteria: “unknown” is valid and leads to uncertainty, not automatic exemption.

title: Privacy and lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: the user can decline marketing and still use the product; consent versions and changes are recorded.

title: Reassessment
acceptance_criteria: changed location, activities or employee count produces a dated comparison and preserves user-created tasks.

title: Structured catalogue
acceptance_criteria: incomplete evidence or failed publication gates prevent release; no professional reviewer identity is fabricated.

title: Useful discovery
acceptance_criteria: combinations, pagination, reset and no-results suggestions work without exposing paid source files.

title: Decision-ready detail
acceptance_criteria: higher-risk templates explain when independent advice may be useful and never promise enforceability, suitability or official approval.

title: Safe previews
acceptance_criteria: restricted template content and downloadable masters are absent from public bundles, page source and unauthorised storage responses.

title: Owned downloads
acceptance_criteria: successful exports appear in the business library and remain linked to the template version used.

title: Content ownership and licence
acceptance_criteria: source-checked terms pass editorial gates and the product owner accepts commercial terms before sales; counsel sign-off is not required by this plan.

title: Version and withdrawal handling
acceptance_criteria: an update never silently rewrites a customer’s saved document.

title: Government forms are separate
acceptance_criteria: any downloadable government form has checked reuse rights, provenance and a current-link warning.

title: Saved items and coverage
acceptance_criteria: favourites persist across devices and deleted records degrade gracefully.

title: Guided forms
acceptance_criteria: required placeholders cannot be omitted silently, and inappropriate clauses are not selected solely from a broad industry label.

title: Canonical document model
acceptance_criteria: preview, DOCX and PDF use the same saved revision, not three independently generated texts.

title: Review and editing
acceptance_criteria: changes remain after reload and login on another device; locked guidance is distinguished from editable business content.

title: Autosave and concurrency
acceptance_criteria: two open tabs cannot silently overwrite each other; retry preserves unsaved text in memory.

title: Missing-data protection
acceptance_criteria: final export blocks mandatory omissions or requires a deliberately watermarked incomplete draft; never invent legal names, addresses or signatures.

title: Real file generation
acceptance_criteria: each guided template opens in Word and a standard PDF reader; long names, multi-page tables and the naira symbol render correctly. [S22–S23]

title: Durable export jobs
acceptance_criteria: worker restart does not lose the job and repeated requests do not create uncontrolled duplicate exports.

title: Private retrieval
acceptance_criteria: expired/revoked access fails; browsers and shared caches do not retain private responses as public assets.

title: Bounded formatting
acceptance_criteria: unsupported content cannot trigger remote network fetches or code execution.

title: Ownership after changes
acceptance_criteria: revoking platform access is never described as retracting a previously downloaded local file.

title: Supported tasks and user control
acceptance_criteria: unsupported customer legal requests are directed to a scoped published resource, official authority or independent adviser; no adviser availability is implied.

title: Bounded generation
acceptance_criteria: invalid output is retried once under policy, then fails safely with the manual editor available.

title: No invented business facts
acceptance_criteria: the model cannot invent a tax rate, registration number, approval, signature or payment receipt.

title: Governed applicability
acceptance_criteria: ungrounded claims and unreleased rules never enter live assessments.

title: Privacy-aware input
acceptance_criteria: test payloads prove only the selected document context is transmitted and no customer content enters generic analytics.

title: Injection and tool controls
acceptance_criteria: prompts cannot override permissions, change policy or execute unauthorised actions.

title: Traceability and quotas
acceptance_criteria: a quota breach stops new AI calls without blocking manual document access.

title: Customer drafting quality gate
acceptance_criteria: at least 95% meet the rubric, every financial calculation is correct and no critical leak or invented legal claim remains. Keep this separate from the editorial suite in EDP-010; neither measures certified legal accuracy.

title: Graceful failure
acceptance_criteria: a model outage does not break paid downloads, free guidance or the deterministic editor.

title: Required content structure
acceptance_criteria: missing authoritative evidence, scope or review manifest blocks publication of the affected claim; a human reviewer is not a required field.

title: Applicability language
acceptance_criteria: no output states that the business is legally exempt or fully compliant merely because a questionnaire did not trigger a rule.

title: Federal, state and local separation
acceptance_criteria: a Lagos-only entry cannot appear as a national requirement, and an unknown LGA never receives invented local obligations.

title: Sources and review dates
acceptance_criteria: labels say “AI reviewed” or “Source checked”; “professionally reviewed” appears only if that review actually occurred and was recorded.

title: Legal updates and historic periods
acceptance_criteria: running the same profile under two rule versions remains reproducible and explains changed recommendations.

title: Deadlines and fees
acceptance_criteria: missing evidence shows “Confirm with the authority”; an assumed due date is never scheduled automatically.

title: Freshness and conflicts
acceptance_criteria: stale or unresolved numeric rules cannot generate definite recommendations or new statutory reminders; show an uncertainty notice and official route.

title: AI editorial control
acceptance_criteria: separate drafting and review runs plus deterministic gates control automated publication. No Nigerian specialist or second human approval is required; a named owner can pause or withdraw content.

title: Free and understandable
acceptance_criteria: the source and basic guidance remain readable without purchase and are not disguised professional endorsements.

title: Configurable questionnaire
acceptance_criteria: irrelevant questions are skipped, progress is clear, and the user can return to previous answers.

title: Unknown is a first-class state
acceptance_criteria: missing turnover, workforce or location information generates a follow-up or uncertainty label, never an exemption.

title: Deterministic rules
acceptance_criteria: equal input, assessment date and released ruleset version give equal results; arbitrary code is rejected.

title: Explainability
acceptance_criteria: every recommendation exposes a plain-English “Why am I seeing this?” explanation.

title: Threshold-safe evaluation
acceptance_criteria: a broad turnover band that straddles a threshold requests more information instead of forcing a result.

title: Complete but bounded results
acceptance_criteria: coverage gaps and excluded high-risk sectors are visible; no compliance score implies a legal certification.

title: Versioned assessment records
acceptance_criteria: users can compare assessments; anonymous answers are cleared unless they explicitly choose to save.

title: Regression and boundary tests
acceptance_criteria: all critical results and exclusions pass; unresolved interpretations remain held.

title: Safe updates and scheduling
acceptance_criteria: a rule change flags existing tasks for review rather than silently deleting or backdating them.

title: Business workspace
acceptance_criteria: all data survives refresh and device changes; localStorage is limited to non-sensitive display preferences.

title: Personal task tracking
acceptance_criteria: a user-completed item is never described as accepted by a regulator.

title: Reminders
acceptance_criteria: duplicate scheduler runs do not duplicate messages; unknown statutory dates cannot become automatic deadlines.

title: Delivery preferences
acceptance_criteria: unsubscribe and preference changes are enforced before dispatch, not just when the job was created.

title: Private evidence boundary
acceptance_criteria: upload controls are absent or disabled. Evidence uploads are R2 and require malware scanning, access controls and retention review.

title: Activity and support
acceptance_criteria: logs omit draft bodies and unnecessary personal details; support confirms receipt only after the ticket is durably saved.

title: Service discovery
acceptance_criteria: service pages are useful even when no provider is listed and do not imply government affiliation.

title: Real enquiries
acceptance_criteria: the user sees “Enquiry received”, not “Appointment booked”; failed dispatch is visible to staff.

title: Verified profiles only
acceptance_criteria: no fictional provider, fabricated rating or unsupported “accredited” claim reaches production.

title: Future bookings
acceptance_criteria: booking or payment controls remain feature-disabled until that gate is approved.

title: Server-priced orders
acceptance_criteria: a client-modified amount, currency, product or discount cannot alter the charged order.

title: Hosted checkout
acceptance_criteria: Valo never stores card numbers, security codes or payment credentials; live and test modes use isolated keys and data.

title: Authoritative confirmation
acceptance_criteria: a browser success URL alone cannot unlock a template.

title: Webhook authenticity
acceptance_criteria: invalid, replayed and duplicate events cannot create a new purchase.

title: Atomic fulfilment
acceptance_criteria: callback and webhook races, retries and worker restarts create one grant only.

title: Pending and failed payments
acceptance_criteria: interrupted browser sessions recover their purchase without requiring an unnecessary second payment.

title: Reconciliation
acceptance_criteria: finance can resolve a discrepancy with an audit trail and without editing financial history directly.

title: Refunds and disputes
acceptance_criteria: a refund is not marked complete when merely requested; entitlement effects are explicit and user-owned drafts are not silently deleted.

title: Receipts and licence access
acceptance_criteria: a generated business invoice is never confused with proof of payment or an official government tax invoice.

title: No unapproved billing expansion
acceptance_criteria: later billing products require approved economics, terms, failure handling and their own migration/reconciliation tests.

title: Operational console
acceptance_criteria: a finance user cannot read document bodies and an author cannot change payment configuration.

title: Editorial workflow
acceptance_criteria: retain model/run IDs, findings, evidence, hashes and timestamps. A separate publisher service releases only eligible versions; no per-item human approval is needed and a drafting run cannot approve itself.

title: Source registry
acceptance_criteria: a source change opens AI drafting/review and validation jobs; publication follows only after every gate passes, not directly from a crawler alert.

title: Rule publishing
acceptance_criteria: failed critical tests block release and prior versions can be restored without losing assessment history.

title: Template release control
acceptance_criteria: every published item has an immutable eligible version and reproducible export tests; specialist sign-off is not an acceptance dependency.

title: Commercial configuration
acceptance_criteria: historic orders retain their original terms and values after pricing changes.

title: Safety switches
acceptance_criteria: free unaffected guidance remains available and the reason, actor and customer impact are recorded.

title: Support escalation
acceptance_criteria: anyone can report an error free of charge; unresolved items are held or withdrawn without waiting for an unavailable specialist.

title: Audit integrity
acceptance_criteria: application users cannot modify audit history; tampering and excessive privileged access generate alerts.

title: Permitted publication scope
acceptance_criteria: publication needs no human signature per item, but cannot expand its own scope.

title: Evidence collection
acceptance_criteria: failed retrieval, unclear amendments or missing operative provisions hold affected claims rather than generating substitutes.

title: AI drafting
acceptance_criteria: invented citations, business facts and rights assertions fail validation.

title: Separate AI checks
acceptance_criteria: unexplained disagreement holds release. Model agreement is not independent professional validation.

title: Enhanced checks
acceptance_criteria: a material uncertainty holds the whole template or inseparable rule; detachable unsupported claims may be removed and the complete item rechecked.

title: Mechanical validation
acceptance_criteria: every mandatory check passes on the exact candidate version. A model’s confidence or pass verdict cannot override a failed deterministic check.

title: Publication manifest
acceptance_criteria: edits, expired evidence, failed tests or a changed policy invalidate eligibility and return the item to review; no per-item human approval is required.

title: Transparent public status
acceptance_criteria: no “lawyer approved”, “professionally verified”, “guaranteed compliant” or equivalent claim without actual supporting review.

title: Least privilege automation
acceptance_criteria: injection, forged manifests and direct publish attempts fail and are logged.

title: Editorial evaluation
acceptance_criteria: zero critical false publications and at least 95% overall; no claim of a legal-accuracy percentage.

title: Monitoring and correction
acceptance_criteria: withdrawal reaches search, caches, downloads and checker; past customer files are never silently rewritten.

title: Holds and accountability
acceptance_criteria: owners cannot waive a failed mandatory gate.

title: Separated environments
acceptance_criteria: no live personal data is seeded into dev; integration tests cannot charge production accounts.

title: Request and worker separation
acceptance_criteria: export, reminder and reconciliation jobs survive web-app scale-down and worker restarts. Deployment behaviour must be proven, not assumed. [S10–S11]

title: Controlled schema deployment
acceptance_criteria: one authorised migration owner; no competing automatic schema-push paths. [S12]

title: Secrets and account ownership
acceptance_criteria: no keys in prompts, browser bundles, commits or screenshots; rotation and emergency revocation are rehearsed.

title: Supply-chain and code review
acceptance_criteria: the release identifies commit, migration, content/rule versions and known issues.

title: Hosting and data geography
acceptance_criteria: no claim that Nigerian customer data stays in Nigeria without proof. [S10]

title: Production compatibility spike
acceptance_criteria: failures produce an approved architecture change before core implementation scales.

title: Safe rollback
acceptance_criteria: deploy the previous application version safely or restore through a tested recovery plan; irreversible migrations require a separate approved runbook.

title: Object-level authorisation
acceptance_criteria: automated negative tests enumerate cross-tenant ID substitutions across all private entity types.

title: Transport, storage and secrets
acceptance_criteria: no secret-bearing client bundle; sensitive backups and storage objects are not publicly addressable; rotation tests pass.

title: Input and output controls
acceptance_criteria: stored/reflected XSS, injection and cross-site mutation tests pass.

title: Renderer and network isolation
acceptance_criteria: document text cannot fetch cloud metadata, local files, private URLs or execute embedded script/macros.

title: Abuse and quotas
acceptance_criteria: legitimate errors explain recovery; distributed abuse and financial-cost spikes trigger alerts.

title: Privileged operations
acceptance_criteria: no actor bypasses content gates or accesses private drafts without permission; automation cannot grant roles, change policy or suppress its own audit evidence.

title: Vulnerability management
acceptance_criteria: no open critical or high exploitable issues in launch paths, with lower-severity exceptions owned and time-bound.

title: Monitoring and response
acceptance_criteria: a tabletop incident demonstrates containment, evidence preservation, privacy escalation and customer communications.

title: Processing inventory
acceptance_criteria: the privacy notice reflects actual production processing and optional consent is not bundled with required service terms.

title: Processors and transfers
acceptance_criteria: documented review covers Replit, identity, email, payments, AI and monitoring; no unverified “zero retention” promise. [S10, S18]

title: Individual rights and incidents
acceptance_criteria: a test request traverses all systems. Notification triggers/deadlines must have retrieved statutory evidence and AI checks; the privacy owner owns incident decisions. Uncertainty prompts immediate assessment and authority contact, not an invented deadline.

title: Availability
acceptance_criteria: External synthetic checks; incident log; documented denominator and planned-maintenance treatment.

title: Public performance
acceptance_criteria: Pre-launch lab checks plus real-user measurements when a sufficient sample exists; disclose sample size.

title: API and search
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible test excluding AI/render duration but including application authorisation and database work.

title: Export and AI
acceptance_criteria: Job telemetry, timeout/failure cases and content-format comparison; queue time included.

title: Recovery
acceptance_criteria: Restore into isolated environment, verify data/permissions and replay reconciliation; provider backup capability proved.

title: Accessibility
acceptance_criteria: Automated checks plus manual keyboard and assistive-technology review. [S20]

title: Browsers and mobile
acceptance_criteria: Document supported-version matrix, real-device checks and touch interaction tests.

title: Localisation
acceptance_criteria: Timezone-boundary and naira/export glyph tests; unknown dates remain unset.

title: Reliability
acceptance_criteria: Concurrency, network-loss, webhook-race, worker-crash and database-failure tests.

title: Operability
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic failures verify alerts, redaction and support escalation.

title: Maintainability
acceptance_criteria: CI report plus scenario tests; coverage percentage never substitutes for negative security cases.
